title: Network Performance and Capacity
summary: Compare bandwidth, throughput, latency, packet loss, utilization, and reserve using synthetic telemetry.
objectives: Distinguish bandwidth, throughput, latency, packet loss, utilization, and availability.
Use synthetic interface data to identify congestion risk and remaining headroom.

vocab.def: The amount of data successfully moved over a period of time.
The time required for data to travel between endpoints.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Telemetry in this activity is synthetic. Do not capture traffic or inspect unauthorized systems.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: A link can have high bandwidth but lower measured throughput. Latency describes delay; packet loss describes data that did not arrive; utilization describes how much capacity is in use. Interpret all signals together instead of treating the highest number as failure.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Calculate simple reserve from stated capacity and observed demand, then identify what remains uncertain.

practice.prompt: Can low latency prove that throughput is adequate?
practice.answer: No. Latency and throughput are different measures and must be considered with demand and other evidence.

quiz.question: What is packet loss?
options: Data that did not arrive at the destination
quiz.answer: Data that did not arrive at the destination

reflectionPrompt: Which signal showed a constraint, and what evidence would confirm it?
